gallery.title.situation: Heading shown above the image grid/list once the batch is non-empty (Functional Design §3.2, 'Populated state'). Sits above the mono meta line (image count and total input size) and above the toolbar row (Add images / Add folder / Clear / view mode toggle).
gallery.title.control: Static heading text, not an interactive control. Reads naturally as a possessive noun phrase in English ('Your Images'); translators are free to restructure into whatever phrasing a section title takes in the target language.

action.compressLabel.situation: Label on the single primary action button that starts a compression run (Functional Design R-A1). {count} is the number of images currently in the batch; the button is only ever shown with count >= 1, since it is disabled and unreachable when the batch is empty.
action.compressLabel.control: The one primary call-to-action button in the app: solid tint-red, always visible (panel footer on desktop, fixed bottom bar on mobile). Must read as a verb followed by a parenthesised count, e.g. 'Compress (6)' — translators should keep the count in parentheses rather than folding it into a full sentence, because it sits inside a fixed-width button, not a paragraph.

panel.section.quality.situation: Section heading above the Quality controls (target selector, slider, LOW/MED/HIGH shortcut chips) in the side panel (Functional Design §4.1). Sibling headings in the same visual family are Dimension and Format (§4.2, §4.3) — not yet added as keys, but translators should expect this word to read consistently with those when they arrive.
panel.section.quality.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking (Functional Design §14.2, 'Section headings are uppercase with wide tracking'). Not a button — do not translate as a call to action.

panel.section.dimension.situation: Section heading above the Dimension accordion (Original size / Fit within long edge / Fixed width / Fixed height rows) in the side panel (Functional Design §4.2, docs/ui-design.md §9). Sibling of panel.section.quality and panel.section.format — should read consistently with both.
panel.section.dimension.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking, same treatment as panel.section.quality. Not a button.

panel.section.format.situation: Section heading above the output-format dropdown in the side panel (Functional Design §4.3, docs/ui-design.md §10). Sibling of panel.section.quality and panel.section.dimension — should read consistently with both.
panel.section.format.control: Static section heading, rendered uppercase with wide letter-tracking, same treatment as panel.section.quality. Not a button.

shell.breadcrumb.selected.situation: Header breadcrumb (docs/ui-design.md §2) shown while the Gallery stage mode is mounted. {count} is the number of images currently in the batch, including zero for the empty state.
shell.breadcrumb.selected.control: Mono, uppercase (applied via CSS text-transform, not baked into this string), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.preview.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while the Preview stage mode is mounted, for the one image currently being previewed. {filename} is that image's original file name, user data, so it must not be uppercased by this template — CSS text-transform handles the surrounding label text only in visual effect, but since the whole line is one uppercase run, translators should not add casing logic around {filename} either; it renders however the surrounding CSS transform renders the whole string.
shell.breadcrumb.preview.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.edit.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while the Edit stage mode is mounted, for the image currently being rotated/cropped. {filename} is that image's original file name (user data).
shell.breadcrumb.edit.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.breadcrumb.processing.situation: Header breadcrumb shown while a compression run is in progress (Processing stage mode).
shell.breadcrumb.processing.control: Mono, uppercase (CSS text-transform), small text next to the wordmark. Not interactive.

shell.optionsButton.situation: Mobile-only header button (docs/ui-design.md §2) that opens the settings drawer. Rendered next to a decorative menu glyph (☰) that is not part of this string — the glyph is marked aria-hidden and carries no translatable text of its own.
shell.optionsButton.control: Solid tint-red pill button, same visual weight as the primary Compress action. This is the button's full visible label, so it also serves as its accessible name (R-K10) — no separate aria-label is added.

shell.hideButton.situation: Sticky button pinned to the top of the mobile settings drawer (docs/ui-design.md §2) that closes it. Rendered next to a decorative arrow glyph (→) that is not part of this string.
shell.hideButton.control: Small button at the top of the drawer's scroll area. This is the button's full visible label and accessible name (R-K10) — no separate aria-label is added.

shell.panelLabel.situation: Not visible text — the accessible name (aria-label) for the side panel landmark, used identically whether it renders as the static desktop column or the mobile drawer (docs/ui-design.md §2). Lets a screen-reader user identify the region without relying on its visual position.
shell.panelLabel.control: ARIA label on a region/dialog container, never rendered as visible text.

shell.modeNotYetBuilt.situation: Placeholder body text shown inside each of the four stage-mode components (Gallery/Preview/Edit/Processing) as built by T31, before T33-T38 give each one real content. Temporary — removed as each mode's real task lands.
shell.modeNotYetBuilt.control: Plain paragraph text inside the stage body.

gallery.emptyState.headline.situation: The large headline inside the empty-state drop zone that covers the whole stage when the batch has no images (Functional Design §3.2). Shown alongside the formats line and two Select buttons.
gallery.emptyState.headline.control: Large, bold display text, centred. Not interactive.

gallery.emptyState.formats.situation: A mono line below the empty-state headline naming the formats this build accepts as input (R-I1). Rendered as a middle-dot-separated list; translators should keep format names as their common technical abbreviations (JPEG, PNG, ...) rather than translating them, and may keep or substitute the '·' separator with whatever list punctuation reads naturally.
gallery.emptyState.formats.control: Small, quiet mono text. Not interactive.

gallery.emptyState.selectImages.situation: Primary button inside the empty-state drop zone that opens the file picker for individual images (R-I24 and its sibling flat-selection entry point).
gallery.emptyState.selectImages.control: Solid tint-red pill button, the empty state's main call to action. This is the button's full visible label and accessible name (R-K10).

gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.situation: Secondary button inside the empty-state drop zone that opens the folder picker (R-I24). Hidden entirely on a platform where folder selection is unavailable (R-I31) rather than shown disabled.
gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.control: Outlined button next to Select images. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.addImages.situation: Toolbar button in the populated Gallery state (Functional Design §3.2) that adds more individual images to the existing batch via the file picker. Same underlying action as gallery.emptyState.selectImages, different surrounding chrome (a small toolbar button rather than the empty state's large primary button), so it may read more tersely.
gallery.toolbar.addImages.control: Small outlined toolbar button. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.addFolder.situation: Toolbar button in the populated Gallery state that adds more images from a folder to the existing batch. Hidden when folder selection is unavailable (R-I31), same as gallery.emptyState.selectFolder.
gallery.toolbar.addFolder.control: Small outlined toolbar button. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.clear.situation: Toolbar button that removes every image from the batch and returns to the empty state, with no confirmation prompt (R-G6 — re-selecting files is cheap, and a confirmation dialog costs more on a touch device than the mistake it guards against).
gallery.toolbar.clear.control: Small quiet toolbar button, visually de-emphasised relative to Add images/Add folder since it is destructive. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.viewToggleLabel.situation: Accessible group label for the grid/list view-mode toggle in the Gallery toolbar (R-G7). The app auto-selects an initial mode by file count and folder origin (R-G8); this control lets the user override it for the session.
gallery.toolbar.viewToggleLabel.control: role="group" wrapper around the two toggle buttons. Not itself visible text — an aria-label only.

gallery.toolbar.viewGrid.situation: One of the two grid/list view-mode toggle buttons (R-G7). Selects the thumbnail grid.
gallery.toolbar.viewGrid.control: Small toggle button with aria-pressed reflecting whether grid is the active view. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.toolbar.viewList.situation: One of the two grid/list view-mode toggle buttons (R-G7). Selects the no-thumbnail list view (R-G9), grouped by directory for folder input (R-G11).
gallery.toolbar.viewList.control: Small toggle button with aria-pressed reflecting whether list is the active view. Full visible label and accessible name.

gallery.meta.situation: Mono meta line beneath the 'Your Images' title in the populated Gallery header, shown above both the grid and list views (docs/ui-design.md §6, 'Populated header row'). {count} is the current batch size and {size} is the total input size using the UI size formatter, never a size estimate — nothing has been compressed yet.
gallery.meta.control: Small mono text beneath the title. Not interactive.

gallery.affordance.situation: One line of guidance shown above the grid/list body in the populated Gallery header (docs/ui-design.md §6), telling the user what clicking a tile or row does before they've tried it.

gallery.badge.edited.situation: Tile/row badge shown when an image has a stored rotation or crop (R-G4). Appears first when more than one badge applies (docs/ui-design.md §6: EDITED → ANIMATED → FAILED).
gallery.badge.edited.control: Small text label with its own background, not a colour-only indicator (R-K10's colour-never-alone rule). Not interactive.

gallery.badge.animated.situation: Tile/row badge shown when the source is a multi-frame image that will be written as an animated output format. Second in display order when more than one badge applies.
gallery.badge.animated.control: Small text label with its own background, same treatment as gallery.badge.edited. Not interactive.

gallery.badge.failed.situation: Tile/row badge shown when processing failed for this image (Functional Design §10). Last in display order when more than one badge applies.
gallery.badge.failed.control: Small text label with its own background, same treatment as gallery.badge.edited. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.dimensionPending.situation: Placeholder shown in place of the W×H figure while the background dimension probe (T33-A) has not yet resolved this image's size. Replaced in place once the probe resolves or fails.
gallery.tile.dimensionPending.control: Inline text inside the tile's mono meta line. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.dimensionError.situation: Shown in place of the W×H figure when the background dimension probe could not read this image's size at all. Distinct from gallery.tile.dimensionPending — this is a terminal state, not a still-resolving one. The image itself may still be processed; only the displayed dimensions are affected.
gallery.tile.dimensionError.control: Inline text inside the tile's mono meta line. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.meta.situation: The tile's 'W×H · size' line (docs/ui-design.md §6). {dimensions} is either the real W×H figure or one of gallery.tile.dimensionPending/dimensionError, already resolved to text before this template runs; {size} uses the UI size formatter. One template per R-L5, not a concatenation of two translated fragments.
gallery.tile.meta.control: Small mono text beneath the filename. Not interactive.

gallery.tile.remove.situation: Accessible name for each tile's remove (×) control, top-right (docs/ui-design.md §6). {filename} disambiguates one tile's remove button from every other tile's in the same grid for a screen-reader user, since the visible glyph alone does not. Clicking it does not open the tile's Preview and does not affect any other tile (R-G2).
gallery.tile.remove.control: Small icon-only button with no visible text label, so this string is its aria-label rather than a redundant addition to visible text (R-K10).

panel.quality.targetGroupLabel.situation: Accessible group label for the two-button Quality/Size segmented toggle at the top of the side panel's Quality section (Functional Design §4.1, docs/ui-design.md §8). Not visible text — read by assistive technology to identify the group, same role as gallery.toolbar.viewToggleLabel.
panel.quality.targetGroupLabel.control: aria-label on a role="group" wrapping two aria-pressed buttons. Should name what the two buttons choose between, not describe the buttons themselves.

panel.quality.targetQuality.situation: Label on the first of the two Quality/Size segmented-toggle buttons (Functional Design §4.1). Selecting it switches the panel to show the quality slider instead of the size-target field.
panel.quality.targetQuality.control: Button text inside a two-option segmented control. Short — sits in a fixed-width pill alongside 'Size'.

panel.quality.targetSize.situation: Label on the second of the two Quality/Size segmented-toggle buttons (Functional Design §4.1). Selecting it switches the panel to show the numeric size-target field and KB/MB toggle instead of the slider.
panel.quality.targetSize.control: Button text inside a two-option segmented control. Short — sits in a fixed-width pill alongside 'Quality'.

panel.quality.sliderLabel.situation: Accessible name for the quality range slider (10–100), shown only when the Quality target is active (Functional Design §4.1). The numeric value itself is displayed separately in a large mono readout above the slider, not part of this string.
panel.quality.sliderLabel.control: aria-label on a native <input type="range">. Should read as what the slider controls, not include the current value or range.

panel.quality.chipLow.situation: One of three shortcut chips above the quality slider that jump the slider to a preset value (Functional Design §4.1: LOW 40 / MED 70 / HIGH 90). Clicking it sets the slider to 40; the slider remains freely adjustable afterward.
panel.quality.chipLow.control: Chip button text. The number is part of the fixed English label per the design table, not a separate interpolated value — keep 'LOW' and '40' together as translators see fit for their language's convention.

panel.quality.chipMed.situation: One of three shortcut chips above the quality slider (Functional Design §4.1: LOW 40 / MED 70 / HIGH 90). Clicking it sets the slider to 70.
panel.quality.chipMed.control: Chip button text, same treatment as panel.quality.chipLow.

panel.quality.chipHigh.situation: One of three shortcut chips above the quality slider (Functional Design §4.1: LOW 40 / MED 70 / HIGH 90). Clicking it sets the slider to 90.
panel.quality.chipHigh.control: Chip button text, same treatment as panel.quality.chipLow.

panel.quality.sizeFieldLabel.situation: Accessible name for the numeric text field where the user types a target file size, shown only when the Size target is active (Functional Design §4.1). The KB/MB unit is a separate adjacent toggle, not part of this field's value.
panel.quality.sizeFieldLabel.control: aria-label on a numeric <input>. Should name what the number represents, not include the unit.

panel.quality.unitGroupLabel.situation: Accessible group label for the KB/MB segmented unit toggle next to the size-target field (Functional Design §4.1). 'KB' and 'MB' themselves are not translated — they are the standard byte-unit abbreviations, same convention as domain/sizes.ts's report/UI size formatters.
panel.quality.unitGroupLabel.control: aria-label on a role="group" wrapping two unit-toggle buttons.

panel.dimension.groupLabel.situation: Accessible group label for the four-row Dimension radio accordion (Functional Design §4.2, docs/ui-design.md §9). The section already has a visible 'DIMENSION' heading (panel.section.dimension) rendered by SidePanelSection; this is a separate string read by assistive technology directly on the radio group, since an <h2> is not programmatically associated with the group it introduces.
panel.dimension.groupLabel.control: aria-label (or <legend>-equivalent) on the radio group wrapping the four dimension rows.

panel.dimension.rowOriginal.situation: First row of the Dimension accordion (Functional Design §4.2): the default, no-op dimension rule. Selecting it means the batch's output keeps each image's original pixel size (subject to per-image crop, R-D1).
panel.dimension.rowOriginal.control: Radio row label, clickable text next to a radio dot. No value field or chips appear under this row when selected.

panel.dimension.rowFitLongEdge.situation: Second row of the Dimension accordion (Functional Design §4.2): downscale-only rule bounding the image's longer edge to a pixel value the user enters or picks via a shortcut chip (HD/FHD/2K/4K/IG).
panel.dimension.rowFitLongEdge.control: Radio row label. When selected, reveals a numeric pixel field and five shortcut chips.

panel.dimension.rowFixedWidth.situation: Third row of the Dimension accordion (Functional Design §4.2, R-N1, R-N2): sets output width to an exact value (upscaling or downscaling as needed), deriving height to preserve aspect ratio.
panel.dimension.rowFixedWidth.control: Radio row label. When selected, reveals a numeric pixel field and four shortcut chips (IG/WEB/MAIL/PRINT).

panel.dimension.rowFixedHeight.situation: Fourth row of the Dimension accordion (Functional Design §4.2, R-N1, R-N2): sets output height to an exact value, deriving width to preserve aspect ratio.
panel.dimension.rowFixedHeight.control: Radio row label. When selected, reveals a numeric pixel field and three shortcut chips (IG/HD/FHD).

panel.dimension.chipHd.situation: A shortcut chip that writes a preset pixel value into the active Dimension row's numeric field (Functional Design §4.2's chip table). 'HD' is reused across two different rows with two different values (1280 on Fit within long edge, 720 on Fixed height) via {value} — the abbreviation itself is translated once here.
panel.dimension.chipHd.control: Chip button text, e.g. 'HD 1280'. {value} is a plain pixel number, not locale-formatted (matches gallery.tile dimension display convention).

panel.dimension.chipFhd.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation 'FHD' (Full HD), reused across the Fit within long edge row (1920) and Fixed height row (1080) with different {value}s. Same mechanism as panel.dimension.chipHd.

panel.dimension.chip2k.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation '2K', used only on the Fit within long edge row (value 2560).

panel.dimension.chip4k.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation '4K', used only on the Fit within long edge row (value 3840).

panel.dimension.chipIg.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation 'IG' (Instagram), reused across three rows with three different {value}s: Fit within long edge (1080), Fixed width (1080) and Fixed height (1350).

panel.dimension.chipWeb.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation 'WEB', used only on the Fixed width row (value 1200).

panel.dimension.chipMail.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation 'MAIL', used only on the Fixed width row (value 800).

panel.dimension.chipPrint.situation: Shortcut chip abbreviation 'PRINT', used only on the Fixed width row (value 3000).

panel.dimension.noteMultiCropped.situation: R-D2's note, shown above the Dimension accordion when the batch has more than one image and at least one carries a crop. {count} is how many images in the batch are cropped (can be less than the total batch size) — those images take their output size from their own crop and ignore the row selected below; the rest still follow it.
panel.dimension.noteMultiCropped.control: Informational note text, not a button. Exact wording is specified in docs/ui-design.md §9: "Crop applied to N images. Their crop overrides the setting below; the rest follow it."

panel.dimension.noteSingleCropped.situation: R-D3's note, shown in place of the accordion (which becomes fully disabled) when the batch has exactly one image and it is cropped — that image's crop already fixes its output size, so there is nothing left for the Dimension rows to control.
panel.dimension.noteSingleCropped.control: Informational note text, not a button. Exact wording is specified in docs/ui-design.md §9.

panel.format.selectLabel.situation: Accessible name for the output-format <select> dropdown (Functional Design §4.3, docs/ui-design.md §10). The section already has a visible 'FORMAT' heading (panel.section.format); this is a separate string read directly on the control, since an <h2> is not programmatically associated with the <select> it introduces.

panel.format.optionDontChange.situation: The default, first entry in the output-format dropdown (Functional Design R-F1, §4.3): each image keeps its own input format independently rather than being converted. The other five options (JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF/GIF) are format names/acronyms and are deliberately left untranslated, same convention as domain/sizes.ts's KB/MB — this is the one option that is an actual sentence fragment needing translation.
panel.format.optionDontChange.control: <option> text. Should read as an instruction not to convert, distinct from naming any specific format.

panel.format.gifWarning.situation: Inline warning note shown beneath the format dropdown only while GIF is the selected output format (Functional Design §4.3: "Produces worse results than JPEG for photographs, stated inline in the dropdown"; docs/ui-design.md §10 places the same copy as inline warning text rather than inside the <option> itself, since <option> text can't carry secondary styling).
panel.format.gifWarning.control: Informational note text, not a button.

action.meta.multiOriginal.situation: Primary action meta line (Functional Design §4.4, R-A2, R-F4) for a batch of more than one image with the format setting on 'Don’t change'. {count} is the batch size. Shown beneath the Compress button's label, states facts only — never an estimated output size.
action.meta.multiOriginal.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button. Exact wording per docs/ui-design.md §10 example: '6 images · Original formats · ZIP'. 'Original formats' itself is not re-translated here — it's baked into this template rather than composed from panel.format.optionDontChange, since R-L5 forbids building a sentence by concatenating two translated fragments.

action.meta.multiFormat.situation: Primary action meta line for a batch of more than one image with a concrete format selected. {count} is the batch size; {format} is the chosen format's acronym (e.g. 'WEBP'), supplied already uppercased and not itself translated (see panel.format.optionDontChange's note on format acronyms).
action.meta.multiFormat.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button. Exact wording per docs/ui-design.md §10 example: '6 images · WEBP · ZIP'.

action.meta.singleOriginalWithDimensions.situation: Primary action meta line for a single-image batch with the format setting on 'Don’t change' and the image's output pixel size already known. R-F4 applies unconditionally on batch size, so this still reads 'Original formats' rather than naming the one concrete format that would actually be produced. {width}/{height} are the resolved output dimensions (accounting for any crop or the batch dimension rule), not the raw source size.
action.meta.singleOriginalWithDimensions.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button, e.g. 'Original formats · 1920×1440'.

action.meta.singleOriginalPending.situation: Same as action.meta.singleOriginalWithDimensions, but for the moment before the single image's dimensions have been probed (width/height still unresolved, gallery.tile.dimensionPending's same 'not yet known' state) — the pixel figure is omitted rather than shown as a placeholder.
action.meta.singleOriginalPending.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button, e.g. just 'Original formats'.

action.meta.singleFormatWithDimensions.situation: Primary action meta line for a single-image batch with a concrete format selected (or resolved, e.g. an animated source substituted to WebP per R-F6, or an unencodable source falling back to JPEG per R-F2). {format} is the real resolved output format's acronym, already uppercased. {width}/{height} are the resolved output dimensions.
action.meta.singleFormatWithDimensions.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button. Exact wording per docs/ui-design.md §10 example: 'WEBP · 1920×1440'.

action.meta.singleFormatPending.situation: Same as action.meta.singleFormatWithDimensions, but before the single image's dimensions have been probed — the pixel figure is omitted.
action.meta.singleFormatPending.control: Small mono meta text under the primary button, e.g. just 'WEBP'.

preview.frame.creating.situation: Shown in the Preview frame, in place of the compressed image, while a real encode of the current image is running (R-P1: "the app immediately begins encoding and shows a Creating preview state in the frame"). Also appears on every settings change, because the previous result is discarded at that moment rather than left on screen as a stale picture (R-B1). Announced to assistive technology as a live status (R-K5).
preview.frame.creating.control: Status text centred in the stage frame. Not interactive.

preview.frame.ready.situation: Announced to screen-reader users the moment an encode finishes, since the change is otherwise only visual: the image appears and the size figures return (R-K5). Never shown to sighted users — the image itself is the visible signal.
preview.frame.ready.control: Visually hidden live-region text. Not interactive.

preview.frame.altOriginal.situation: Alternative text for the Preview frame's image while the Original tab is selected. {filename} is the user's own file name. The image is the content of the screen here, not decoration, so it carries real alternative text rather than an empty alt.
preview.frame.altOriginal.control: The alt attribute of the image element in the stage frame.

preview.frame.altCompressed.situation: Alternative text for the Preview frame's image while the Compressed tab is selected (the default, R-P2). {filename} is the user's own file name — the input name, since this is the same picture rather than a different file.
preview.frame.altCompressed.control: The alt attribute of the image element in the stage frame.

preview.frame.originalUnavailable.situation: Shown in place of the Original tab's image when the browser cannot decode the source file itself — a HEIC on Chromium or Firefox, a TIFF, a JPEG XL. The compressed result is unaffected, because the app decodes those formats itself; only the browser's own rendering of the untouched original is missing. This is deliberately not papered over by transcoding the source to a browser-renderable format just to display it: that would show the user a lossy stand-in and call it 'Original'. Instead this names the file, states the real reason (R-E1), and mentions the desktop application — one of Functional Design §1.3's three named cases ('formats the browser cannot decode') where the limit is the browser's, not this product's, same convention as R-I21.
preview.frame.originalUnavailable.control: Note text centred in the stage frame, in place of the image. Not interactive.

preview.error.decode.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame when decoding the image fails (Functional Design §10, "Corrupt or undecodable file"). Shown with a retry action beside it. Names the file and says what is wrong rather than "something went wrong" (R-E1).
preview.error.decode.control: Error text inside the stage frame, above a retry button.

preview.error.encode.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame when the encode fails (Functional Design §10, "Encode failure → Run or preview → in Preview, an inline error in the frame with a retry"). Says what to change, since the settings are reachable without leaving Preview.
preview.error.encode.control: Error text inside the stage frame, above a retry button.

preview.error.memory.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame when the browser runs out of memory compressing this image (Functional Design §10, "Out of memory"). Mentions the desktop application because the limit is the browser's rather than a product decision (R-I21).
preview.error.memory.control: Error text inside the stage frame, above a retry button.

preview.error.unsupported.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame for a combination the pipeline does not implement yet — today, an image whose colour is signalled only as CICP values going to a format that cannot carry them. {format} is the output format acronym, already uppercased and not itself translated. Says which control to change (R-E1).
preview.error.unsupported.control: Error text inside the stage frame, above a retry button.

preview.error.sourceMissing.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame when the image's stored file cannot be found at all — a state no normal interaction produces, kept as a named message so it can never surface as a blank frame or a generic failure (R-E1).
preview.error.sourceMissing.control: Error text inside the stage frame, above a retry button.

preview.error.retry.situation: The retry action beside an inline Preview error, which runs the same encode again (Functional Design §10 requires a retry on a Preview encode failure).
preview.error.retry.control: Button with visible text, so it needs no separate accessible name (R-K10).

preview.comparison.toggleLabel.situation: Accessible name for the whole Original/Compressed comparison pill, which is one switch rather than two buttons — clicking anywhere on it flips the view (Functional Design §3.3). Read together with its on/off state, this is what tells a screen-reader user which view is active, which the two visible words alone cannot (R-K6).
preview.comparison.toggleLabel.control: The aria-label of a single switch control. Its visible text is the two view names plus the size figures, so a separate name is warranted here (R-K10).

preview.comparison.original.situation: The left half of the comparison pill in Preview, selected when the frame is showing the untouched source image (Functional Design §3.3).
preview.comparison.original.control: Text inside one half of a two-state pill. The halves are not separately clickable; the whole pill toggles.

preview.comparison.compressed.situation: The right half of the comparison pill in Preview, selected by default once the encode finishes (R-P2).
preview.comparison.compressed.control: Text inside one half of a two-state pill. The halves are not separately clickable; the whole pill toggles.

preview.comparison.reduction.situation: The trailing figure of the comparison pill when the compressed file is smaller than the original. {percent} is a positive whole number. The down glyph is part of the string because the direction must not be carried by colour alone (R-K8).
preview.comparison.reduction.control: Small mono figure at the end of the comparison pill, in the tint colour (§14.1 reserves tint for the reduction figure).

preview.comparison.reductionUnderOne.situation: Replaces preview.comparison.reduction when the saving is real but rounds to less than one percent, so the figure is never shown as a flat 0%.
preview.comparison.reductionUnderOne.control: Small mono figure at the end of the comparison pill, in the tint colour.

preview.comparison.increase.situation: The trailing figure of the comparison pill when the compressed file is *larger* than the original — a legitimate result of changing format or of lossless settings. R-P5 requires it to be shown as an increase with an up glyph and a non-tint colour, and never suppressed or shown as zero.
preview.comparison.increase.control: Small mono figure at the end of the comparison pill, in ordinary text colour rather than tint, with the up glyph carrying the direction as well (R-K8).

preview.comparison.increaseUnderOne.situation: Replaces preview.comparison.increase when the file grew by less than one percent. R-P5 forbids showing an increase as zero, which rounding alone would do.
preview.comparison.increaseUnderOne.control: Small mono figure at the end of the comparison pill, in ordinary text colour.

preview.comparison.unchanged.situation: The trailing figure of the comparison pill when the compressed file is exactly the same number of bytes as the original. No glyph, because nothing moved.
preview.comparison.unchanged.control: Small mono figure at the end of the comparison pill.

preview.transform.line.situation: The Preview transform line (Functional Design §3.3), describing this one image: its own name and pixel size, then the output name and pixel size the current settings produce. Driven by the settings rather than by the encode, so it updates while an encode is still being debounced. One whole template rather than assembled parts (R-L5).
preview.transform.line.control: One line of small mono text below the comparison pill. Not interactive.

preview.transform.lineNoSizes.situation: The transform line before this image's pixel dimensions are known (the background probe has not reached it yet). The names and the output extension are already correct, so the line is shown without the figures rather than with placeholders.
preview.transform.lineNoSizes.control: One line of small mono text below the comparison pill. Not interactive.

preview.transform.flatten.situation: Shown under the transform line when the chosen output format cannot store transparency, so any transparent pixels will be filled instead (R-C17: "where transparency will be flattened, the Preview transform line says so"). {format} is the output format acronym, already uppercased and not itself translated. Worded as something that *will* happen because whether this image actually has transparent pixels is not measured until it is compressed — the report states the measured outcome afterwards.
preview.transform.flatten.control: Small muted note under the transform line. Not interactive.

preview.transform.animationSubstituted.situation: Shown under the transform line when the image is animated and the chosen output format cannot hold animation, so WebP is written instead of dropping the frames. R-F6 requires the substitution to be stated on the tile, on this line, and in the report. WebP is a format name and is not translated.
preview.transform.animationSubstituted.control: Small muted note under the transform line. Not interactive.

preview.toolbar.back.situation: Preview toolbar action returning to the Gallery with the batch and settings intact (Functional Design §3.1's transition table, docs/ui-design.md §11).
preview.toolbar.back.control: Button with visible text, so it needs no separate accessible name (R-K10).

preview.toolbar.addMore.situation: Preview toolbar action opening the file picker from inside Preview (R-M3). If the batch then holds more than one image the app returns to the Gallery (R-M2), so this action can take the user off this screen.
preview.toolbar.addMore.control: Button with visible text, so it needs no separate accessible name (R-K10).

preview.toolbar.edit.situation: Preview toolbar action opening Edit mode for the image on screen, shown when that image has no stored rotation or crop yet (docs/ui-design.md §11).
preview.toolbar.edit.control: Button with visible text, so it needs no separate accessible name (R-K10).

preview.toolbar.editChanges.situation: Replaces preview.toolbar.edit once the image already carries a stored rotation or crop, so the label says the edit will be revisited rather than started (docs/ui-design.md §11).
preview.toolbar.editChanges.control: Button with visible text, so it needs no separate accessible name (R-K10).

preview.toolbar.editAnimatedReason.situation: Shown beside a disabled Edit button when the image on screen is animated. R-C16 removes editing for animated sources in this version and requires the reason to be stated inline rather than leaving a control that silently does nothing.
preview.toolbar.editAnimatedReason.control: Small muted note in the Preview toolbar, beside the disabled Edit button.

preview.toolbar.stepper.situation: The Preview stepper's position readout, between the previous and next controls, shown only when the batch holds more than one image (docs/ui-design.md §11). {index} is 1-based.
preview.toolbar.stepper.control: Small mono text with tabular figures so the digits do not jitter when stepping. Not interactive itself.

preview.toolbar.previous.situation: Accessible name for the Preview stepper's back control, which wraps to the last image from the first (R-P7). The visible glyph alone does not say what it does.
preview.toolbar.previous.control: Icon-only button, so this string is its aria-label (R-K10).

preview.toolbar.next.situation: Accessible name for the Preview stepper's forward control, which wraps to the first image from the last (R-P7). The visible glyph alone does not say what it does.
preview.toolbar.next.control: Icon-only button, so this string is its aria-label (R-K10).

preview.error.animatedAvif.situation: Inline error in the Preview frame for an animated AVIF, which has no encode path at all (R-F7, R-F8). R-F8 wants this rejected at selection time with the reason named, and that rejection list is T39's work — until it exists, such a file can still reach Preview, and this message is what keeps that from being a silent failure. Names the file and what to do next (R-E1).
preview.error.animatedAvif.control: Error text inside the stage frame. No retry is offered with it, because retrying cannot change the outcome.
